title: Discovery and first clinical use of insulin
summary: At the University of Toronto, Frederick Banting, Charles Best and J. J. R. Macleod began experiments on 17 May 1921 to extract a blood-sugar-lowering substance from the pancreas, and James Collip later purified it. In January 1922 Leonard Thompson, aged 14, became the first person to receive insulin; Banting and Macleod shared the 1923 Nobel Prize.

uncertainty.note: The record spans the research from 17 May 1921 to the first injections of January 1922 (11 and 23 January).

as_recorded.value: On 17 May 1921 Banting, Best and Macleod first got together to begin their research
11 January 1922 – insulin was first used to treat a person with diabetes
Beginning on January 11, 1922, insulin (initially called isletin) was administered to 14-year old Leonard Thompson

where.modern_name: University of Toronto, Toronto, Ontario, Canada
where.historical_name: University of Toronto (research) and Toronto General Hospital (first injection), Toronto, Ontario, Canada

importance.justification: Made insulin available as a treatment for diabetes, saving millions of lives.
